question: Doubling the dose of a statin from its standard dose to its maximum dose produces an approximately 50% additional reduction in LDL-C.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The statin dose-response relationship is logarithmic, not linear. Doubling the dose adds only ~6% more LDL lowering (the 'rule of 6s'). For patients not at LDL target on a moderate-intensity statin, adding ezetimibe is far more effective than simply doubling the statin dose.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. This is the statin dose-response plateau: doubling the statin dose adds only approximately 6% further LDL-C reduction (the 'rule of 6s'). Therefore, if the LDL-C target is not met at standard doses, adding ezetimibe (which provides ~15–20% additional reduction) is more effective than further dose escalation.
